result.verdict: Not ready. The switch breaks in four places: lines 1-3 are three mediums in a row, and line 3 is where I would scroll. Lines 8-10 and 17-19 are strings of 2-word bits labelled M. issues.problem: This is the third medium in a row after his own two lines (8, 12, then 13 words), and the longest line so far. It only describes the scene. The monsters from line 2 disappear for 5 seconds, and it says 'fire' twice. On (d): yes, 'priests chanting around the fire' gives the picture. But 'big fire ceremony' alone can read as a bonfire, a Hindu wedding, or (for Thai viewers) monks chanting at a cremation. 'Teacher is doing a big fire ceremony' also clashes with line 7's 'not one word': how does he do a chanting ceremony without a word? Fix: make the priests the ones who chant, call it 'mantra' (every Ashtanga student chants one, and it is the book's word, 1.30.10 'mantravat'), and split the line into short then medium.

(b) First scroll point: v3 line 3, at about 0:07.5. It is the third long line in a row. The two boys and the monsters from line 2 disappear for 5 seconds while the scene is described. Lines 1-2 (his own) hold.

(d) Line 3 clarity: mostly yes, but only by explaining. 'Priests' alone can read as Christian (and Orthodox for Russian viewers). Fire with monks or priests chanting reads as a cremation to a Thai viewer. 'Chanting mantra' makes it Indian and yogic at once, and Ashtanga students chant a mantra themselves. In the fix the picture comes first (fire, priests, mantra) and the word 'ceremony' only comes at line 7, so by then the viewer knows what it means. Keep the teacher OUT of the chanting: he is under the mauna vow (1.30.4). Never say 'teacher chanting'.

result.notes:
I checked against the Rao word-by-word file for Bala 30 (live_balasans30.htm, verses 1 to 26, read in full) and Griffith Canto XXXII (pg24869.txt lines 4845 to 4948).

LINE 3, 'priests chanting around the fire': supported.
- Rao 1.30.8: 'brightening the chief officiator of the ritual, namely Vishvamitra, and other priests around it.'
- Rao 1.30.9: 'around which Vishvamitra and the conductors of ritual are sitting.'
- Rao 1.30.10: mantravat, 'according to hymnal rendering'.
- Griffith: 'Round priest and deacon...' and 'With sacred texts began anew.'
- The line has the priests chanting, not the teacher, so it does not clash with his silence. Keep it that way: never 'the teacher chanting'.

LINE 5, 'the boys walk around the fire, bows ready... six nights, no sleep': supported.
- Rao 1.30.6: 'alertly patrolling nearby the Altar of Fire', 'wielders of great bows' (gloss 'nearby they moved - patrolled').
- Rao 1.30.5: 'wakefully safeguarded ... for six nights and days' (anidrau = without sleep).
- Griffith: 'disdaining sleep, / Six days and nights their watch to keep.'
- The checked translation supports moving about near the fire better than his 'sitting staring at fire'. 'Walk around' should be heard as 'move about near it', not as walking in a circle around the fire as part of the ritual.

LINE 7, 'He promise... not one word until the ceremony is done': fair to the vow.
- Rao 1.30.4: 'under the vow of ritual goes into muteness as required by the vow.'
- Griffith: 'The saint his Dikshá has begun, / And all that time will speak to none.'
- In Rao, the first time he speaks after the vow is 1.30.25, 'On the completion of ritual'.
- In the book it is the other sages who tell the boys this. Line 7 is narration and does not say whom he spoke to or refused, so Flag 8 holds. The card A VOW OF SILENCE keeps the silence a vow and not coldness.

LINE 9, 'Something wrong?': safe. It has no subject, it is a question and not a claim, and line 19 answers it ('Five quiet days... that was the practice'). It puts no thought in the boys' heads. In the book they are eager for the fight (1.30.3), not worried, so no line should say 'the boys worry'. Delivery tip, not required: start the lens look on line 9 rather than line 10, so the question is clearly his.

LINE 18, 'finally... speak again': supported by 1.30.25. Vishvamitra says nothing between 1.30.4 and 1.30.25. The praise in 1.30.24 comes from the other sages.

OTHER STORY LINES:
- Line 4: 1.30.2, and the translator's note under 1.30.8 says 'to spoil the ritual'.
- Line 11: 1.30.7.
- Line 12: 1.30.10 to 11, and Griffith 'roar' and 'vast clouds'.
- Line 14: 1.30.18.
- Line 15: 1.30.20.
- Line 16: 3.42.
- Line 17: 1.30.25 to 26 (same day, near evening prayer time).

- No killing is said or shown.
- ONE ARROW and 'Rama shoot one arrow' never say 'only'.
- Maricha is not named in speech or on screen.
- 'Years later' has no number.
- The movie is small on-screen text only (line 2). Per Flag 13, check a Bangkok showtimes page again if the Reel goes up after about 25 Nov.
- Vishvamitrasana · Advanced A is a name link only.
- The word 'pose' does not appear; it is 'asana' everywhere.
- Indian names only, no episode number, Thai sign-off kept.

Line 22, 'that silent teacher': this is fine as a name link, because the only claim is 'named after', and 'silent' just points back to the teacher in this story. If it stays (it is cut in the length fix), 'Named after that teacher.' removes any hint that the asana is about silence. That is optional.

- Lines 3 and 5 both say 'around the fire' one after the other. 'So the boys guard the fire, bows ready...' keeps the fact (1.30.6, 'protected') and removes the echo.
- Lines 3 and 5 are 13 words each, against the brief's limit of about 12.
